---
description: "How NCodeGroup repositories keep XML doc comments, code comments, OpenAPI metadata, contract catalogs, changelogs, runbooks and pending-work tracking accurate and in step with the code they describe."
applyTo: "**/*.cs, **/*.md, **/*.csproj, **/*.ts, **/*.tsx, **/*.js, **/*.tf, **/.github/workflows/*.yml, **/CHANGELOG.md"
---

# Documentation

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **When a change renames, re-signatures or changes the behavior or design of a type, member or contract, update every place that refers to it in the same change: callers, overloads, tests, XML docs, code comments, README and other Markdown docs, and decision records.** References that fall out of sync leave contradictions between files. Docs and comments that still describe an old or insecure design mislead the next reader, and the fix has to live in the repository, not only in chat history. *Check:* For each renamed, re-signatured or behavior-changed item in the diff, search for callers, tests, `///` and `//` comments, Markdown and ADRs that still use the old name or describe the old behavior. <sub>NCodeGroup maintainer: gap-hunting-review; Identity repository.instructions.md</sub>
- **When a change adds or renames a field, field-name constant or event type in a documented record or wire contract, such as an audit record or event catalog, update the contract document or shipped catalog in the same change, and name new event actions according to the documented taxonomy.** The contract document is the reviewed contract that log pipelines, sinks, dashboards, alerts and runbooks are built against, so the event set has to change on purpose and must not drift from the code. *Check:* Look for new or renamed record fields, field-name constants, event types or action names with no matching edit to the contract doc or catalog, and for action names that don't follow the documented naming scheme. *Note:* In NCode Identity the event-action taxonomy is dotted, for example `token.issued` or `auth.failed`. <sub>Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity ADR-0047</sub>
- **When a change adds or renames a meter, instrument, span, attribute or attribute value, update the package's telemetry/metrics catalog documentation in the same change. A new span should name or add the histogram it mirrors, and the catalog should document both using the same vocabulary.** The catalog is the reviewed contract that dashboards and alerts are built against, and it describes traces and metrics with one vocabulary. *Check:* Look for diffs that add or change `Meter`/`Create*` calls, `ActivitySource` span names, or metric tag names or values without a matching edit to the metrics catalog doc. <sub>Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-0298</sub>
- **Declare every non-200 response of a minimal-API endpoint with `.Produces(StatusCodes.StatusNNN)` or `.Produces<T>()`. Use `<response code>` XML docs only to describe a response that is already declared.** A `<response>` XML tag does not add a response to the OpenAPI document, so a response documented only that way never appears in it. *Check:* Look for `<response code="4xx">` or other non-200 response tags that have no matching `.Produces` call on the endpoint. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **For a minimal-API handler's XML docs to reach its OpenAPI operation, the defining project must reference Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi and call `AddOpenApi`, the handler must be `internal` or more visible, and the endpoint must not also use `.WithSummary()` or `.WithDescription()`. Use either fluent metadata or XML docs for an operation, never both.** The XML-comment source generator silently ignores private handlers and skips operations that already carry fluent metadata. *Check:* Look for private handlers with `///` docs, endpoints that combine `.WithSummary`/`.WithDescription` with XML docs, and handler projects that have docs but no OpenApi package reference or `AddOpenApi` call. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Declare the bearer security scheme in the OpenAPI document, plus the OAuth2 flow when one applies, and reference it from every authenticated operation.** API reference renderers such as Scalar need the scheme to show an authentication control and attach the token to requests. *Check:* Look for new authenticated endpoints, or OpenAPI configuration, that do not declare or reference a security scheme. <sub>Identity ADR-0044</sub>
- **Keep internal references out of `///` doc comments: no ADR numbers, no relative links to repository docs, no persistence column names, no internal implementation type names. Put any ADR reference in a `//` comment instead.** `///` text ships to consumers through IntelliSense XML and OpenAPI schema descriptions, where internal references mean nothing or are broken links. *Check:* Look for `///` comments containing 'ADR-', `<see href="../`, database column names, or the names of internal types. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under `## [Unreleased]`, in the same pull request, for every consumer-visible change to public API, behavior or configuration.** Consumers rely on the changelog to learn what changed, and that knowledge has to live in versioned repository content. *Check:* Look for public API, behavior or configuration changes with no matching CHANGELOG.md update in the diff, and for entries added outside `## [Unreleased]`. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity repository.instructions.md</sub>
- **Add each CHANGELOG entry exactly once, in the correct section, and make sure scripted or automated insertions did not copy it under every heading with the same name.** Inserting before a heading text that appears many times has copied the same entries into every `### Changed` section. *Check:* Look in CHANGELOG diffs for the same entry text repeated across several sections or releases. <sub>Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Track deferred work and follow-ups as GitHub issues. In code comments, refer to the issue as `issue #123`. In Markdown, use a full link of the form `[#123](https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/issues/123)`. Never use hand-allocated IDs or untracked TODO, FIXME or 'remaining' notes.** GitHub issues are the single source of truth for pending work. A reference by issue number stays valid and connects the item to the pull request that completes it. *Check:* Look for new TODO, FIXME, 'deferred', 'follow-up' or 'remaining' comments or bullets with no issue reference, references that use a home-grown ID scheme, and Markdown that gives a bare `#N` without an issue link. <sub>Identity ADR-0264; Identity repository.instructions.md</sub>
- **Do not add or keep backlog, TODO-list or follow-up catalogs of pending work in repository files. File each item as its own GitHub issue and link to it instead.** Markdown catalogs with hand-allocated IDs collide across concurrent branches, need text moved between files to mark an item complete, and can't link an item to the pull request that closes it. The repository holds conventions and reasoning, not a backlog. *Check:* Look for diffs that add backlog or follow-up sections or files listing pending items in Markdown instead of linking to issues. <sub>Identity ADR-0264</sub>
- **A pull request that completes a tracked pending-work item includes `Closes #N` in its description, and removes any doc text that still frames the item as pending.** An item is done when the merged pull request closes its issue, which makes completion a single fact anyone can check, and an item must never be both done and still described as pending. *Check:* For a pull request that removes an `issue #N` reference or implements the work it describes, check that the description contains `Closes #N` and that no 'still open' bullets remain. <sub>Identity ADR-0264; Identity repository.instructions.md</sub>
- **Do not ship a partial implementation of deliberately deferred functionality. Leave a comment at the place where it would go, and have that comment reference the tracking issue.** A deferred feature needs its own review. The note marks where the additive change goes without shipping unreviewed code. *Check:* Look for half-implemented deferred features, and for extension points kept for planned features that have no comment pointing to an issue. *Note:* Identity ADR-0011 marks these places with a `// Future:` comment. The more recent ADR-0264 requires pending work to reference a GitHub issue, so a `// Future:` marker should also carry `issue #N`. <sub>Identity ADR-0011; Identity ADR-0264</sub>
- **When a project turns off a source generator or analyzer as a workaround, for example `EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=false`, add a comment next to the setting that explains why and names the guard test and the decision record or tracking issue for turning it back on.** The opt-out is meant to be temporary, for example until the Request Delegate Generator honors antiforgery validation, so the setting must point to the tests that make re-enabling safe and to the issue that tracks it. *Check:* Look for `EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=false`, or a similar opt-out in a .csproj, with no nearby comment naming the guard test and the ADR or issue. <sub>Identity ADR-0262</sub>
- **When a change alters infrastructure, required manual settings, token permissions or steps that an operational runbook describes, update the runbook in the same change.** The runbook must stay accurate for anyone rebuilding the platform from scratch, so it has to change together with what it describes. *Check:* Look for diffs to bootstrap infrastructure code, workflow permissions or required settings with no matching edit to the runbook that documents them. <sub>Identity docs/platform-bootstrap.md</sub>
- **When a change introduces or relies on a new convention, a non-obvious design decision or a recurring tooling gotcha, record it in the repository's versioned docs in the same change: scoped instruction files for conventions, an ADR for the reasoning, the AGENTS/CONTRIBUTING guide for build or orientation knowledge. Chat, a wiki, personal notes or agent memory are not enough.** Knowledge kept outside the repository isn't versioned or reviewed, so it drifts from the code and has to be learned again and again. *Check:* Look for diffs that set up a new pattern or work around a quirk in a non-obvious way without updating instruction files, ADRs or AGENTS/CONTRIBUTING docs, and for PR text that cites a rule that exists only in chat, a wiki or memory. <sub>Identity ADR-0008</sub>
- **Give every type or member you add, or whose signature or behavior you change, a `///` XML doc comment. Do not add doc comments to undocumented code the change doesn't otherwise touch.** New and changed API must be documented. Existing undocumented code is grandfathered so that diffs stay focused. *Check:* Look for new or modified public/internal types or members without `///` docs, and for diffs that add docs to members they don't otherwise touch. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Mark a type that is public only for cross-assembly infrastructure with `[EditorBrowsable(EditorBrowsableState.Never)]`, and open its summary with the standard 'supports the infrastructure and is not intended to be used directly from your code' boilerplate.** This follows the EF Core and ASP.NET Core pattern and keeps infrastructure types out of what application code sees. *Check:* Look for public types used only by infrastructure that lack the attribute or the boilerplate summary. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Write `///` and `//` comments and ADR prose in the timeless present. Avoid change-relative words such as 'now', 'new', 'previously', 'no longer', 'renamed' or 'moved', and never name a removed or renamed identifier.** History belongs in Git and the CHANGELOG. The text must read correctly to someone who never saw the earlier version. *Check:* Look for comments with temporal or change-relative wording, and for comments that refer to a deleted or superseded type or member by its old name. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Write a substantive `<summary>` that explains purpose, behavior and context, and use `<param>`, `<returns>` and `<remarks>` where they add clarity.** A one-line summary that only repeats the member name gives consumers no useful context. *Check:* Look for summaries that only restate the member name, and for missing param or returns docs where they would help. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Start a property summary with 'Gets or sets', 'Gets' or 'Sets' to match its accessors, and use 'Gets' for an `init`-only property.** This is the Microsoft convention, and an init-only property is read-only after construction. *Check:* Look for `{ get; init; }` or get-only properties documented as 'Gets or sets', and for property summaries that don't use these openings. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Write comments that explain why, not comments that restate what the code does, and do not leave commented-out code.** Comments that restate the code add noise, and Git already keeps the history of removed code. *Check:* Look for comments that paraphrase the next line of code, and for blocks of commented-out code. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **In comment prose, spell protocol terms the way their specifications do, for example 'JSON Web Token (JWT)', JSON, JOSE, OAuth and OpenID, not in the Pascal casing of a .NET type name. cref targets and identifiers keep their real casing.** Documentation should use the specifications' standard terminology. *Check:* Look for `///` or `//` prose that writes 'JsonWebToken', 'Json', 'Jose', 'Oauth' or 'OpenId' as a plain word. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **To have an API reference renderer pre-check and pre-fill an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` request field, mark the field `required` and set its schema `Default` in the OpenAPI document. Do not rely on named examples being applied to form fields.** Renderers such as Scalar build form bodies from schema properties. Optional properties render unchecked and are left out of the request, and named examples aren't applied, so the form ends up empty. *Check:* Look for OpenAPI transformers that try to pre-fill form-urlencoded fields only through named examples, or that leave those fields optional. <sub>Identity ADR-0046</sub>
- **Put the `<summary>` opening tag, its content and its closing tag on separate lines, even when the summary is short.** This keeps doc comment formatting consistent. *Check:* Look for a single-line `/// <summary>...</summary>`. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
